name: worktrunk
description: Git worktrees for your agents, through Worktrunk (wt): list, create, switch, merge and remove worktrees, start a chat in a new one, and keep Worktrunk installed and up to date.

tools.name: list
tools.description: List the repository's git worktrees with Worktrunk: each branch, its folder, how far it is ahead of or behind the default branch, uncommitted changes and its last commit. The chat's own worktree is marked @. Without repo, the chat's own repository.

repo.description: Full path of a git repository or one of its worktrees. Default: this chat's folder.

branches.description: Also list branches that have no worktree.

full.description: Also fetch CI status and summaries (slower, uses the network).

tools.name: status
tools.description: This chat's own worktree: its branch, folder, changes and where it stands against the default branch and its upstream.

repo.description: Full path of a worktree. Default: this chat's folder.

tools.name: create
tools.description: Create a new branch and a worktree for it (wt switch --create), running the repository's approved Worktrunk hooks. Answers the new worktree's folder; this chat's own folder doesn't change, so work there by its full path, or hand the work to a new chat with start_chat.

base.description: The branch to start from. Default: the repository's default branch.

repo.description: Full path of the repository. Default: this chat's folder.

tools.name: switch
tools.description: Make sure an existing branch (or pr:123 / mr:123) has a worktree, creating the worktree if needed, and answer its folder. This chat's own folder doesn't change.

branch.description: The branch, or ^ for the default branch, or pr:N / mr:N for a pull or merge request.

create.description: Create the branch if it doesn't exist.

base.description: With create: the branch to start from.

repo.description: Full path of the repository. Default: this chat's folder.

tools.name: remove
tools.description: Remove worktrees by branch (wt remove). A branch already merged into the default branch is deleted too; an unmerged one is kept unless force_delete. A worktree with uncommitted changes is refused unless force (Worktrunk then backs the changes up to refs/wt-backup/<branch>). This chat's own worktree is never removed unless allow_this_chat.

branches.description: The branches whose worktrees to remove.

force_delete.description: Delete the branch even if it is not merged.

keep_branch.description: Keep the branch; remove only the worktree.

allow_this_chat.description: Allow removing this chat's own worktree.

repo.description: Full path of the repository. Default: this chat's folder.

tools.name: merge
tools.description: Merge a worktree's branch into the target branch locally with Worktrunk (wt merge): commit what's uncommitted, squash, rebase, run the approved pre-merge hooks (tests, lints), fast-forward the target, then remove the worktree. Never pushes. Merging this chat's own worktree keeps it unless remove: true.

target.description: The branch to merge into. Default: the default branch.

branch.description: The branch to merge. Default: the one checked out in repo (this chat's).

rebase.description: Rebase onto the target first (default true).

remove.description: Remove the worktree after merging (default true, except for this chat's own).

stage.description: What to stage before committing (default all).

repo.description: Full path of the worktree to merge from. Default: this chat's folder.

tools.name: start_chat
tools.description: Start a new chat in a worktree: creates the branch and its worktree (or uses the existing one with create: false), then starts a chat there with the prompt. The new chat uses this chat's harness and model unless told otherwise. Use it to hand a piece of work to a parallel agent.

branch.description: The branch for the new chat's worktree.

harness.description: The harness for the new chat (claude, codex, ...). Default: this chat's.

model.description: The model for the new chat. Default: this chat's, on the same harness.

repo.description: Full path of the repository. Default: this chat's folder.

tools.name: version
tools.description: Which Worktrunk is installed, where, how it was installed, its commands, the newest release, and whether an update is out.

check.description: Look up the newest release now (default true; answers are kept for a few hours).

tools.name: help
tools.description: Worktrunk's own help for a command in the installed version (for example ["step"] or ["switch"]). Use it to learn flags and commands this plugin's tools don't wrap, then call run.

command.description: The command words. Empty: the overview.

tools.name: run
tools.description: Run any other Worktrunk command, for example ["step", "diff"], ["step", "prune", "--dry-run"] or ["config", "show"], in the repository. Arguments go to wt as they are, never through a shell. Refused: anything that runs commands or approves hooks without the user (-x/--execute, -y/--yes, --config, --config-set, wt hook, step for-each, step tether, and config changes).

repo.description: Full path of the repository. Default: this chat's folder.

settings.label: Worktrunk program
settings.help: The full path of wt (git-wt.exe on Windows). Empty: the plugin's own copy, else found on PATH or in the usual install folders. Windows Terminal's wt is never used.

settings.label: Worktrunk hooks
settings.help: A repository's hooks (.config/wt.toml) run commands. By default only the ones you approved run (approve them in the Worktrunk view); an unapproved one stops the operation.

settings.label: Harness for new chats
settings.help: The harness a chat started in a worktree uses, for example claude or codex. Empty: an agent's new chat uses the asking chat's; the view's uses claude.

settings.label: Check for Worktrunk updates
settings.help: Look up Worktrunk's newest release every few hours (from its GitHub repository's tags) and show it in the view.
